input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Each call now clears and reuses the single shared statistics dict and binds it into the per-call copy, so overlapping calls of the same decorated function write into one dict and the second call's clear() wipes the first call's in-flight statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at the same time, so the second call reaches stats.clear() while the first is still retrying. Mechanism: before this change each call's copy kept its own statistics dict and only the module-level attribute was rebound; now copy._local.statistics is the same object, so both calls mutate and clear it. Impact: the statistics seen by the concurrent callers (attempt_number, start_time, and similar) are silently wrong or reset mid-call.
critique: The finding describes the same defect as the label. A single statistics dict is shared and cleared on every call, so when calls overlap, the second call's clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number and both callers see wrong statistics.
